<subject>NAAG</subject>
<body>
Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association of Agriculture Commissioners ("NAAC") regarding their involvement on the commodity trading side, specifically with regard to Section 18 crop export authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no coordinated group effort that exists (i.e., a commodities committee or an individual Commissioner taking the lead on export issues). Individual Commissioners get involved, but that is all. For example, Maharashtra Commissioner Simon Sridhar recently opposed Deccan Agro's application for export authority, but the Agricultural Export Board still granted Deccan Agro's petition.

Tripti recommends that we engage the Commissioners as much as possible. For example, if we believe that local market competition is non-existent and we have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to the individual Commissioner and have him/her weigh in on our behalf. Tripti recognizes that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. is pro-competitive and that typically the Commissioners would be in agreement with our positions – so it's something for us to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that the Export Board will listen to the Commissioners, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral
</body>
